title: Stratum Rotor: staged promotion engine with cohort-aware holdpoints and rollback playbook
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce 'Stratum Rotor' rollout engine: deterministic snapshot commits, cohort-aware holdpoints, entropy-based stall detection, session-fenced promotions, and an automated rollback playbook. Backwards compatible; no public API changes.
description:
Title: Stratum Rotor: staged promotion engine with cohort-aware holdpoints and rollback playbook

Summary: Adds a new promotion engine (stratum_rotor) to the rollout subsystem that schedules phased promotions across stratified cohorts (strata). The engine emphasizes deterministic snapshot commits, cohort-aware holdpoints, and an entropy-based stall detector to prevent blind ramping. It also wires a new rollback playbook that integrates offline replay checks and reversible snapshot commits. This PR touches operator, controller, docs, and integration tests.

Motivation and context: We frequently see regressions during aggressive canaries where session stickiness and bursty traffic cause nondeterministic regressions. Current controllers either rely on naive percentage ramps or expensive bisects. Stratum Rotor provides a middle path: staggered strata promotion with session-fencing and silent-window rehearse for low-risk validation, plus an automated rollback advisor when fidelity regressions cross thresholds. Related Linear: ENG-3214, ENG-3491.

What I changed (high level):
- rollout/stratum_rotor.py: core engine implementing strata queues, snapshot commit/abort API, entropy stall detector, and holdpoint logic.
- operator/controllers/promote_controller.go: integrate stratum rotor as an alternate promotion strategy and add license to select strategy via rollout spec.
- docs/rollouts/stratum-rotor.md: architecture, knobs, and recommended release playbook.
- tests/integration/test_stratum_rotor.py: synthetic traffic scenarios (session-coherent, burst, slow-degrade).
- helm/values-rollout.yaml: feature flag and defaults.
- telemetry/metrics.yaml: new metrics (rotor.strata_promote_count, rotor.holdpoint_trigger, rotor.entropy_score, rotor.rollback_advisor_recommend).

Representative commits (squashed on merge):
- 3b6f9a2: initial stratum rotor engine & unit harness
- a47d2c1: integrate engine into operator promote controller; add rollout.strategy.type selector
- 9f2e1b4: add entropy stall detector and silent-window rehearse logic
- 7c5b22f: add offline replay hook & rollback-advisor wiring
- d91e3a0: integration tests + charts + docs

Files changed (illustrative snippets):
- rollout/stratum_rotor.py (new):
  - queue model: strata = [S0, S1, ...] with per-stratum window and session token map
  - commit API: commit_snapshot(snapshot_id) -> atomic on leader, returns checkpoint token
- operator/controllers/promote_controller.go: added switch { case "stratum-rotor": controller = NewStratumRotor(...) }
- docs/rollouts/stratum-rotor.md: contains step-by-step canary template and rollback playbook

- Integration: test suite simulating session-coherent traffic and bursty error injection. One flaky integration (test_replay_race) failed on first CI run; re-ran and passed. CI checks: build, unit, integration, lint, helm-lint (all green on final run).

Operational playbook (short):
1) Start with rollout.spec.strategy: { type: "stratum-rotor", strata: 4, session_fence: true, silent_window: 60s }
2) Monitor rotor.entropy_score and per-strata error rates; holdpoints will pause promotion automatically if entropy_score > 0.7 or error delta > 1.5x baseline.
3) If holdpoint triggered, the rollback advisor will suggest either: (a) rollback last committed snapshot, or (b) replay sampled traffic to the previous snapshot in offline dry-run.
4) Use "redwoodctl rollout snapshot-rewind <id>" to perform an immediate revert if advisor recommends.

Rollback playbook highlights: reversible snapshot commits are stored in the rollout ledger; aborting a commit triggers a coordinated session drain for the target stratum then swaps checkpoint tokens. Offline replay harness runs against sampled requests captured during silent-window and returns a paired diff report.

Backward compatibility: The new strategy is opt-in via rollout.spec.strategy.type and defaults to existing behavior if not set. No public SDK/API changes.

Performance implications: Small additional memory for per-session fencing maps. We measured median latency impact <0.3ms in internal perf lab with 3 strata; tail under control with max-batch-latency knob. See benchmark-lab notes in the PR.

Follow-ups (future work):

- ENG-3710: adaptive strata sizing based on traffic entropy.
